description: LightGBM forecast of calciner outlet temperature (423CI400_TT_4), absolute value 60 seconds ahead. Retrained with CAUSAL (trailing-only) smoothing -- see causal_retrain_note.
trained_by: nn_twin/plc_pipeline.py (sandbox outside this app) -- see backend/forecast.py for the feature engineering reproduced for live inference
target: 423CI400_TT_4 at t+60s (absolute degC, not a delta)

causal_retrain_note.what_changed: nn_twin/plc_pipeline.py's preprocess() previously denoised every tag (including the target) with a CENTERED Savitzky-Golay filter -- using both past AND future samples to smooth 'now'. Live serving structurally cannot do that (no future samples exist yet), so the old training MAE (5.73) never held up live: an independent causal backtest measured ~7-9 degC in that deployment (see git history of this file). Replaced with a trailing (causal-only) rolling mean, CFG.smooth_window=11s, in BOTH training (nn_twin/plc_pipeline.py) and live serving (backend/forecast.py's SMOOTH_WINDOW) -- so this test_metrics.mae is now a fair estimate of live accuracy, not an optimistic upper bound.
causal_retrain_note.why_barely_changed: the leak was in the FEATURE computation (lags/rolling stats built on non-causally-smoothed inputs), not primarily in the sensor-noise reduction itself -- removing it made the number a fraction better here, but the important change is that it is now honest: training and serving compute the identical thing, verified independently below.

known_gaps_in_this_deployment.note: process_live's OPC mapping doesn't carry these 2 of 31 tags. backend/forecast.py imputes them from their process_1min long-run median and flags this in every response's imputed_tags field -- accuracy on live forecasts is degraded relative to test_metrics above until the live feed is remapped to include them.

live_deployment_backtest.how: python -m etl.backtest_forecast -- runs THIS repo's own backend.forecast.forecast_from_recent() (the exact function the live API calls) against real historical 1-second data from CSV_1S_PATH, scored against a causally (trailing-only) denoised actual -- matching the causal target definition, so this is a leakage-free, apples-to-apples check of the retrained model.
live_deployment_backtest.finding: the causal fix closed most of the gap between training and live-serving evaluation (both now compute the same thing), but per-window accuracy still varies a lot with plant regime: 3.66 degC on a calmer afternoon vs 8.29 degC on a more volatile morning. Both windows show a NEGATIVE bias (predictions run low), consistent in direction though not magnitude -- the same non-stationary-drift pattern documented elsewhere in this repo (nn_twin/ LSTM soft sensor, backend/analysis.py's retired point-in-time GBT twin). A fixed additive bias correction was tried previously on the non-causal model and made an out-of-sample window WORSE, so none is applied here either.
live_deployment_backtest.conclusion: honest expected live accuracy is close to the requested ~5 degC on typical/calm periods, degrading toward ~8 degC during faster-moving regimes. Treat 5.69 degC (training) and ~6 degC (2-window empirical average) as the realistic range, not a single guaranteed number -- the Twin Simulator UI's forecast panel states this caveat directly rather than presenting a single number as certain.
